positions.name: OwnedVsRentedIntelligenceAsset
positions.frame: what is retained as the owned asset versus what is merely the commodity substrate, when intelligence is framed in terms of ownership?
positions.why: Both expressions read in the same direction across every dimensional pass that touches them: register marks both as the same aphoristic-technical-maxim signature (a thesis crystallized into a short, plain-spoken, matched-opposition line); value marks both as appealing to the same ownership/autonomy axis (owned intelligence vs. rented intelligence; the asset you keep); style marks src-3's 'asset you keep' as the perspective-as-retained-asset metaphor that completes src-2's antithesis; and conviction marks both at principle-level, unhedged, creed-like statements rather than mere claims. Together they perform one directional read — separating what is commodity (rented substrate) from what is kept (owned perspective) — that neither carries alone as strongly as the pair does. No tension: the two lines complete each other (distinction, then naming of what's retained) rather than opposing.
